outcome: Anal sphincter function (basal pressure, squeeze pressure, anorectal sensation, balloon expulsion time)
cohort: 17 women who had instrumental delivery and 13 women who underwent elective cesarean section.
finding: Women who had instrumental delivery had significantly lower basal and squeeze pressures, and higher balloon expulsion time at 6 months postpartum compared to women who underwent elective cesarean section, suggesting persistent subtle anal sphincter dysfunction.
